items.title: fix(nature-academic-search): authenticate OpenAlex with API key, drop…
items.description:
fix(nature-academic-search): authenticate OpenAlex with API key, drop mailto polite pool

OpenAlex now ignores the mailto parameter and meters usage per API key.
academic_search.py accepts --api-key / OPENALEX_API_KEY and sends it as an
Authorization: Bearer header; mailto is no longer sent (the flag stays as a
no-op for compatibility). 401/403/429 errors now point at the key. Docs
updated and regression tests added.

Closes #279

Xinrui Ma
items.label: commit

items.title: feat(nature-paper2word): add Markdown → Word skill (documentation only)
items.description:
feat(nature-paper2word): add Markdown → Word skill (documentation only)

Adds a documentation-only skill that compiles a Markdown manuscript into a
journal- or school-compliant Word file. The engine is the PyPI package
md-to-word-docx; the skill carries the router only.

- SKILL.md: scenario, manuscript contract, requirements file, export, gates
- README.md / README_EN.md: mirrored entry pages, eight sections each
- manifest.yaml, agents/openai.yaml: manifest and interface metadata
- Registers the skill in the README index and the project site, and adds its
  path to the skill-tooling workflow
items.label: commit

items.title: docs(nature-figure): panel gaps, tick steps, aspect and labelling con…
items.description:
docs(nature-figure): panel gaps, tick steps, aspect and labelling conventions

Let the content set a figure's height within an author's aspect rule (a row
of bar charts reads better wider than 4:3), keep gaps between panels to what
their labels need, set tick values in the data's own steps rather than the
locator's after a resize, and verify the journal's panel-labelling
convention before changing it. In the schematic rules, ask for a sketch
when a layout described in words can be read two ways.

Xinrui Ma
items.label: commit

items.title: docs(nature-figure): measure printed size; connector and label rules
items.description:
docs(nature-figure): measure printed size; connector and label rules

Add to the QA contract a section on the size figure text prints at in the
compiled manuscript: read the caption size from the document class, set
figure text a little below it, and account for the three things that change
the printed size without changing the source (rescaling a tightly cropped
figure to the text width, TeX versus PDF points, x-height differences
between faces). Verify by measuring x-heights on the rendered page. Add a
section on multi-line labels, whose Matplotlib leading varies with the
alignment, and rules on panel titles, legend placement and palettes.

In the schematic style rules, let unconnected lines cross plainly (a gap
reads as a break), attach connectors at the middle, a third or a quarter of
a side, keep them straight with at most one bend and off box edges, space
repeated cards equally, bold only top-level names, and ask when layout
constraints conflict.

Xinrui Ma
items.label: commit

items.title: docs(nature-figure): agent diagrams, implementation check and text rules
items.description:
docs(nature-figure): agent diagrams, implementation check and text rules

Add an "Agent and tool diagrams" section to the vector schematic style
rules: draw an LLM agent as its iterating loop with the tools as callees,
calls leaving the tool-call station and results returning to the
observation station, and retrieval as one more tool call.

Ask the brief to be checked against the implementation (code,
configuration, methods), render and inspect the edited region after every
revision, and add rules on one dark ink, short box text, even justified
spacing, broken crossings, and shared widths for boxes of one role. In
the default stance, do not print a value on every mark.

Xinrui Ma
items.label: commit
